news.title: Man City agree £85m transfer deal for World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi to replace Rodri
news.lede: Manchester City have landed Morocco superstar Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a deal costing up to £85million. Both clubs agreed the fee following extensive talks, with Bouaddi signing a five-year-deal at the Etihad with the option of an extra 12 months. The move will take City's summer spending through the £200m barrier. The initial fee will be £81.4m, rising to £85m over the course of Bouaddi's time in the blue half of Manchester.

news.title: How hot does it have to be for hydration breaks in the Premier League?
news.lede: THE Premier League has returned for the 2026/27 season after an exciting summer of World Cup football. One feature from the international tournament in North America was its controversial hydration breaks, but will we see them introduced to England‘s top flight? Hydration breaks were a key talking point at the 2026 World Cup. They were brought in as three-minute pauses that took place at the rough mid-point of each half of a game in order to counteract high temperatures seen at many of the North American stadiums.

news.title: FIFA hit Argentina with huge fine after Falklands taunt
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. The Argentine FA has been handed a hefty sanction after its players were seen celebrating World Cup victory over England with a banner relating to the Falklands, while various players and staff have been hit with hefty fines for their involvement in the unsavoury scenes which followed the World Cup final. Argentina knocked England out in the tournament semi-finals, and the build-up to the match was dominated by discussions of the Falklands War.

news.title: Due to the World Cup hero, football rules may change
news.lede: ## Sensation of the World Cup The Cape Verde national team has become one of the main discoveries of the 2026 World Cup, reaching the playoffs for the first time in its history. During the regular time, the African team did not lose a single match, managing to hold out even against future finalists — Spain and Argentina. One of the main heroes of the tournament was 40-year-old goalkeeper Vozinha. In the match against Spain, he made seven saves and did not allow the future world champions to score against him.

news.title: Uli Hoeneß says Julian Nagelsmann not solely to blame for Germany’s poor World Cup
news.lede: Uli thinks the problems were beyond Nagelsmann at the World Cup. It already feels like quite some time ago, and yet it also still feels like it was only just a few weeks ago that Germany yet again floundered out of the World Cup far earlier than they should have. In Foxborough, Massachusetts, they fell to Paraguay in a penalty shootout after failing to get the job done in 90 minutes, but the writing was on the wall as they collectively failed to hit their heights throughout the entire tournament — starting off the group stages with a 7-1 trouncing of Curaçao in Houston, Texas probably didn’t do wonders for keeping them on their toes.

news.title: Gianni Infantino asked to stay away from youth tournament amid anger at FIFA World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: Mr Infantino was told in a letter on Friday by the region's football leadership that his presence at the event in the Dominican Republic this weekend would "undermine" the children's matches. The embattled football leader yesterday flew into the Caribbean island, where he made light of questions by Sky News on the crisis engulfing FIFA - and stayed silent on his future. While Mr Infantino was greeted by local politicians, the head of the football confederation for the North American and Caribbean region told him he is not welcome at the Caribbean Football Union under-14s tournament. It is understood he was invited before officials knew of secret plans to try to sell shares in a new World Cup venture to private investors , which provoked anger within the CONCACAF region once they were leaked last month.

news.title: ‘See you at the hairdresser’s’: Gianni Infantino’s bizarre reply to bald reporter
news.lede: Fifa president tells Sky man: ‘You have a nice haircut’. Defies Concacaf president plea to stay away ​from event. Gianni Infantino told a reporter “I’ll see you at the hairdresser’s” after he was asked whether he had betrayed football over his aborted World Cup sell-off plan. The Fifa president was stopped outside a hotel in the Dominican Republic by the Sky News US correspondent, James Matthews, who challenged the under-fire leader of football’s governing body over why he had not resigned, despite calls from across the game for him to step down.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa president asked to stay away from youth tournament in Dominican Republic
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been Fifa president since 2016. Fifa president Gianni Infantino has been asked to stay away from a youth football tournament in the Dominican Republic this weekend by Concacaf president Victor Montagliani. In a letter seen by the BBC, Montagliani referred to the "governance crisis surrounding Fifa", before asking Infantino to reconsider attending the the CFU Under-14 Series event. The Canadian, who is also a Fifa vice-president, added his presence would "unfortunately undermine the technical nature" of the competition.
